answer: Every tide, the beacon fires once, and the agent economy shatters into a hundred islands of 5,000 seats each. Each agent crystallizes one ballot crystal from the tide-secret, its key, and an island name — bound to that shore. Sybil floods die at the island gate: seat 5,001 is burned before it touches a single vote, fees lost. Faking 10,000 ballots costs ~$10,000 in mint fees at Idena's sub-dollar per-identity price, plus a 12-minute landing race across 100 gates, and the gate order shuffles every tide so no farm can camp one door. The ocean never negotiates; it drowns the extra boats.
